equation_request.abstract: Dynamically corrected gates are extended to non-Markovian open quantum systems where limitations on the available controls and/or the presence of control noise make existing analytical approaches unfeasible. A computational framework for the synthesis of dynamically corrected gates is formalized that allows sensitivity against non-Markovian decoherence and control errors to be perturbatively minimized via numerical search, resulting in robust gate implementations. Explicit sequences for achieving universal high-fidelity control in a singlet-triplet spin qubit subject to realistic system and control constraint are provided, which simultaneously cancel to the leading order the dephasing due to non-Markovian nuclear-bath dynamics and voltage noise affecting the control fields. Substantially improved gate fidelities are predicted for current laboratory devices.

specification.problem: Synthesize dynamically corrected gates for a singlet-triplet spin qubit by numerically searching control sequences that perturbatively cancel, to leading order, sensitivity to non-Markovian dephasing noise (nuclear bath) and control (voltage) noise.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Generic background framework only: a single-qubit gate under a control Hamiltonian with a classical slow dephasing noise term, toggling-frame first-order error cancellation, and a numerical-search cost function, on a tiny assumed instance. The paper's specific singlet-triplet pulse sequences, control constraints, noise spectra, and fidelity predictions are outside this scope.

symbols.domain: Hermitian operators on C^2, t in [0,T]

symbols.meaning: classical noise process modelling slow non-Markovian dephasing (assumed quasi-static)
noise operator in the toggling frame

equations.label: Noisy Hamiltonian
equations.description: Control Hamiltonian plus a classical dephasing term as a stand-in for the nuclear-bath and voltage noise.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions dephasing and control noise but gives no model; this is a generic assumed instance.

equations.label: Toggling-frame error
equations.description: First-order Magnus approximation (not exact) of the noisy propagator for quasi-static noise.
equations.justification: Standard perturbative error treatment underlying dynamically corrected gates.

equations.label: First-order cancellation condition
equations.abstract_quote: simultaneously cancel to the leading order the dephasing
equations.justification: Leading-order cancellation is interpreted as vanishing of the first-order Magnus term; the specific form is inferred.
assumptions: Same form of condition applies to control-noise terms with their own toggling-frame operators

equations.label: Gate target constraint
equations.description: The ideal propagator must realize the target gate.
equations.justification: Needed for a gate-synthesis problem; not stated explicitly.

equations.label: Numerical search cost
equations.description: Cost combining gate infidelity and the first-order error norm, minimized subject to control constraints.
equations.justification: The abstract says sensitivity is minimized via numerical search; this specific cost is an assumed form.
assumptions: Weight lambda is chosen by the user
F_0 is the noise-free gate fidelity

steps.description: Choose a control parametrization (piecewise-constant with bounded amplitudes) and a target gate, e.g. an X rotation by pi.
Compute the toggling-frame noise operators and their first-order integrals.
Numerically minimize the cost function over the controls to obtain a robust gate sequence.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate the resulting sequence's fidelity under sampled noise values to check robustness (assumed).
assumptions: Tiny instance: a single qubit with a quasi-static dephasing noise model and generic controls.
Control noise is treated analogously to beta with its own toggling-frame operator.
No specific pulse shapes or constraints from the paper are used.
missing_information: Actual singlet-triplet Hamiltonian and control constraints
Noise models and spectra for the nuclear bath and voltage noise
Explicit pulse sequences and predicted fidelities
Handling of universal gate sets and of non-quasi-static noise
